groups.root_cause: New adapter request (ZCode) outside initial v2.0 adapter scope
groups.decision: wont-fix: defer ZCode adapter past v2.0 per D14
groups.evidence: No code history exists for ZCode (new feature, not a regression). map-I0.md Q1 frames it as scope question; D14 excludes new adapters from initial v2.0 scope.

edits.change: Mark Q1 resolved: ZCode deferred past v2.0, out of scope per D14.

groups.root_cause: PreToolUse hook CPU budget stated only in docs, not CI-enforced
groups.evidence: r4 proposed a <=20ms CPU budget above bare Node but no independent commit quantifies the 55-70ms PreToolUse cost; nothing enforces the number today.

edits.change: Add a CI-enforced perf assertion: PreToolUse hook adds <=20ms CPU over bare Node spawn, not just a documented budget.

groups.root_cause: Windows shell layer choice undecided (map-I0.md Q5), blocking PATH, shim-resolution and hint-cadence sub-issues
groups.decision: closed-by-design with new ADR section: spawn the target binary directly (no shell: false), eliminating Q5
groups.evidence: No commit found for PATH stripping (#1217) or Windows shim resolution (#1208); b3a26354 'fix(windows): run the better-sqlite3 boot-install via node, not npm.cmd+shell (#861 follow-up)' is the existing v1 precedent of avoiding a shell layer on Windows to dodge exactly this class of bug. Owner rule bans fallback chains, so picking one fixed no-shell spawn path (not three shell-specific code paths) is the simplest compliant option and also resolves #1265 (cadence question collapses once there is no shell-specific hint).

edits.change: State ctx_execute always spawns the interpreter binary directly with shell:false on every OS; remove Q5 (git Bash vs PowerShell vs cmd) from open questions, since no shell is invoked.
Close Q5: no-shell direct spawn makes the git-Bash/PowerShell/cmd choice moot.

groups.root_cause: Rust-executor premise does not match v2's actual executor language
groups.decision: wont-fix: premise does not apply, executor stays Node/TS
groups.evidence: No commit found for a Rust executor; nothing in TECH-SPEC proposes rewriting the executor in Rust, so the PR's cwd/sandbox-cleanup concern targets a component v2 does not build.

edits.change: State explicitly that the v2 executor is Node.js/TypeScript, not Rust, to close any future confusion on this point.

groups.root_cause: Stats path opens sibling session DBs read-write instead of read-only
groups.evidence: No matching commit found in cm-main for read-only stats access; no prior v1 fix exists to regress, so this is a fresh v2 requirement, not a fix-regression check.

edits.change: Add GP case: every sibling session DB opened by ctx_stats is opened readOnly and its mtime is unchanged after a stats run.

groups.root_cause: OpenCode 2.x plugin default-export shape unimplemented; duplicate-closed claim (PR #1171) unverified
groups.decision: covered-by-test with new GP case (treat as open, not duplicate-closed)
groups.evidence: No commit found implementing the OpenCode 2.x plugin default-export shape (id + setup); no PR #1171 found in cm-main history (GitHub API disabled, cannot verify merge state from tickets/data/*.json either). map-I0.md's own duplicate-of-#1171 claim is therefore unverified and should not be treated as fixed.

edits.change: Remove the 'duplicate of PR #1171, therefore fixed' assumption; mark both open pending adapter implementation.
Add GP case asserting the plugin module exports {id, setup} per OpenCode 2.x's plugin API.

groups.root_cause: D15 (no external API calls from sandbox) wording vs user-configured fetch proxy (Firecrawl)
groups.decision: wont-fix: D15 as currently worded bans this class of outbound call
groups.evidence: No commit found for Firecrawl integration (never built, a feature request not a regression). The open question is a scope/policy question D15 already answers as worded: any external HTTP call from the sandbox, including to a user's own proxy, is banned.

edits.change: Clarify D15 wording to explicitly state the ban covers any outbound HTTP from the sandbox, not only LLM API calls, so this class of request reads as settled.

groups.root_cause: ctx_batch_execute does not guarantee dedupe of repeated chunks across queries within one call
groups.evidence: No direct commit found; no existing dedupe-on-repeat-chunk logic located for ctx_batch_execute in the time available for this round.

edits.change: Add GP case: identical chunk returned by two queries in the same batch call is deduped, not just across separate calls.

groups.root_cause: Hook launcher binary path: version-manager (#841) pinning vs Homebrew (#1090) literal 'node' conflict
groups.evidence: b1cca82d / aec2b76a / 25ddacc0 'fix(runtime): liveness-guard pinned hook execPath so mise/asdf/nvm Node upgrades don't break hooks (#841)' already establishes a lazy-resolve-at-run-time pattern (not a fixed string at install time). That same pattern, reused for plugin.json's launcher, satisfies both #841 (survives version-manager switches) and #1090 (survives Homebrew upgrades) without a fallback chain.

edits.change: State the launcher command resolves the Node binary lazily at hook-invocation time (reusing the #841 liveness-guard pattern), not a literal 'node' or a fixed execPath string written at install time.

groups.root_cause: Per-session hook-fire throttle needs a D8-compliant (no DB) storage mechanism, distinct from #593's periodic external-MCP nudge
groups.evidence: 752d5236/a14d244a 'fix(routing): re-fire external-MCP nudge periodically, not once per session (#593)' is a related but separate mechanism. D8 bars hooks from using a DB for this kind of state, so the append-only journal (already used elsewhere per D8) is the compliant store.

edits.change: Specify a session-id-keyed marker in the existing append-only journal for the ppid-keyed throttle, kept as a separate mechanism from #593's periodic external-MCP nudge.

groups.root_cause: r2 left #1135 and #1168 in one unassigned generic GP-case bucket with no test name
groups.decision: covered-by-test with new, separately-named GP cases
groups.evidence: r2's bucket line ('Assign each to a GP case ... or mark wont-fix') names no test; this is a deferred TODO, not a verdict.

edits.change: Add GP4 case for #1135: fetch-error path returns a message with no raw Node stack frame (no line starting with 'at ').
Add a separate GP case for #1168: Pi 0.85's real extension-discovery directories are detected, not hardcoded legacy paths.

groups.root_cause: Codex doctor check for hooks-default-on does not read Codex's actual config default
groups.evidence: No git history found for a Codex hooks-default-on doctor check; nothing confirms the doctor reads Codex's real default rather than assuming false.

edits.change: Add GP case: with no [features].hooks key in Codex config, doctor still reports hooks=true, reflecting Codex's real default.

groups.root_cause: Code-fence echo-first-line default behavior: r2 and r3 disagree on the same mechanism (#1067/#1047)
groups.decision: covered-by-test with new GP case; retract r2's closed-by-design for #1067
groups.evidence: r3's own Q2 treats the echo default as explicitly undecided ('Echo default not decided') while r2 separately called #1067 closed-by-design for the identical mechanism -- a self-contradiction in the review chain. No commit adds the echo as a deliberate feature.

edits.change: Merge #1067 into #1047 as one row; retract r2's closed-by-design verdict for #1067 since it contradicts r2/r3's own Q2.
Add GP case: code-fence echo-first-line is off by default, with an optional summary arg to re-enable it.

groups.root_cause: Plan-mode read-only gather tool proposal duplicates host's own plan-mode capability
groups.decision: wont-fix: accept host's own plan-mode prompt instead of adding a new tool
groups.evidence: No ADR commits to a distinct read-only gather tool; map-I2 Q1 itself frames this as a choice between building new vs using what the host already provides. Simplest single path per owner rule 3: use the existing host plan-mode prompt.

edits.change: Close Q1: no new read-only gather tool; rely on the host's plan-mode prompt.

groups.root_cause: ctx_stats cost-event idempotency is not keyed per turn (D17 silent on this)
groups.evidence: tickets/v2-decisions.md D17 only says 'keep only the data ctx_stats needs'; it does not commit to turn-scoped idempotency. No ADR or TECH-SPEC text pins this down for OpenCode step-finish cost events.

edits.change: Add idempotency-key requirement: cost events are keyed by turn id so repeated step-finish events in one turn count once; add the corresponding GP case.

groups.root_cause: ctx_stats reduction_pct formula and denominator are unspecified (D17 silent on this)
groups.evidence: D17 text does not specify a reduction_pct formula or denominator; no unit test or formula spec found in TECH-SPEC.md or any ADR.

edits.change: Add the exact reduction_pct formula (returned bytes counted once in the denominator) plus a unit test for it.

groups.root_cause: Hints can lose to sibling results in a single parallel tool-call batch; this is host batching/read-order behavior
groups.decision: wont-fix: host-side (Claude Code) batching/read-order issue, not fixable in context-mode's own code
groups.evidence: No cm-main commit addresses hint delivery order inside a single parallel tool-call batch. DECISIONS-r3 Q19 settles routing parity (same routing on every agent) but not delivery order, since order is controlled by how the host reads tool_results, not by context-mode.

edits.change: Add a note that Q19 narrows but does not close the parallel-batch delivery-order question; record it as a host limitation, not an open context-mode item.

groups.root_cause: Windows parent-death detection mechanism (Job Object vs polling) for GP9's 3-OS lifecycle coverage
groups.evidence: TECH-SPEC's GP9 already lists #982 in its covered issue set and claims 3-OS coverage. DECISIONS-r3 Q8 already establishes the Job Object pattern for ctx_execute timeouts on Windows; reusing it for parent-death detection avoids the polling/CPU-spin class seen in #999/#985.

edits.change: Name the Windows parent-death mechanism explicitly as a Job Object (per Q8's pattern), not ppid polling, so GP9's claimed coverage is unambiguous.

groups.root_cause: PreToolUse matcher fires on every mcp__ tool instead of only context-mode's own tools
groups.evidence: e479068a and 9f34c6f1 show each new adapter added its own mcp_tool-shaped matcher, growing the surface that fires on unrelated MCP tools. TECH-SPEC's GP3 issue-id list does not include #960 even though it is the exact matcher-over-broad bug.

edits.change: Add #960 to GP3's issue-id list with a case asserting zero hook process spawns for an unrelated mcp__ tool call (e.g. mcp__grafana__get_datasource).

groups.root_cause: ctx_stats redesign (D17) does not assert the session<=project<=all-time ordering invariant
groups.evidence: No v1 commit found for a part>whole stats fix (design flaw, not a patched regression). GP10 currently asserts idempotency only, not the ordering invariant #950's own acceptance criteria require.

edits.change: Add explicit assertion: session_kept_out <= project_total <= alltime_total, and 0 calls implies 0 savings.

groups.root_cause: ctx_execute default timeout value for the #936/#947/#959/#953 family is undecided and unmeasured
groups.decision: covered-by-test with new GP case, pending a measured value
groups.evidence: eea5877b (#406 lineage) removed the fixed timeout, causing #936's hang. DECISIONS-r3 Q8 answers the default-timeout model generally but cites no measured number.

edits.change: Require a cited spike-measured timeout value before closing #936/#947/#959/#953; they already share one GP4/GP9 test surface and must stay merged.

groups.root_cause: Install/upgrade/doctor each resolve an adapter's plugin root independently, risking mismatches
groups.evidence: 98d239b7 'fix(codex): resolve plugin-manager root for doctor and upgrade (#771)' is the proven fix pattern for the identical bug family on Codex; generalizing one resolvePluginRoot(adapter) function reuses that pattern for OpenCode/Windows.

edits.change: Require a single resolvePluginRoot(adapter) function used by install, upgrade, and doctor, generalizing the #771 fix.

groups.root_cause: Session DB cleanup can race a live-PID process's open DB
groups.evidence: dc25a00a introduced session DB cleanup; 4d7a2f4d and 96990b27 generalized and tuned it; the live-PID-vs-cleanup race is a known risk class in this code.

edits.change: Add contract test: the live-PID check runs inside the cleanup transaction, not as a pre-check with a race window.

groups.root_cause: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CONTEXT_MODE_DATA_DIR resolved separately by multiple subsystems
groups.evidence: fa6541fb, fb55ed03, and 0e806c5c each fixed CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR handling piecemeal in storage, cache-heal, and test sandboxing respectively -- three point-fixes for one root cause.

edits.change: Require one resolveConfigDir() module used by storage, stats, cache-heal, and tests, replacing the three independent reads.

groups.root_cause: Nested .gitignore handling for directory indexing is unverified
groups.evidence: Could not locate the dir-walk .gitignore matcher in cm-main in the time available; insufficient archaeology to confirm negation handling exists.

edits.change: Add GP case asserting nested .gitignore files, including negation patterns, are honored during indexing.

groups.root_cause: Native better-sqlite3 dependency conflicts with D2's no-runtime-installs rule and ensure-deps.mjs's self-heal fallback chain
groups.evidence: ensure-deps.mjs was patched for native-binary bugs across 13+ commits over two years (6a7a6b2e through 28d58774), each a point-fix for one host/runtime combination -- exactly the kind of fallback chain the owner rules forbid. D2 ('no runtime installs') plus 'no npm for v2' together require v2 to either drop the native dependency (pure-JS/WASM sqlite) or ship a prebuilt binary per platform at install time, not reproduce ensure-deps' self-heal chain.

edits.change: State explicitly that v2 either uses a pure-JS/WASM sqlite or ships prebuilt native binaries per platform at install time; ensure-deps.mjs's runtime self-heal chain is not carried into v2.

groups.root_cause: D4 'one fixed source per adapter' wording vs OpenCode clientInfo detection and Pi per-session workspace resolution
groups.evidence: No commit changes this; map-P0.md's existing Contradictions entry already resolves #1276/#1234 by reading D4 as 'one fixed detection method per adapter', which covers OpenCode's clientInfo and Codex's rollout-timestamp. The same reading extends to Pi's per-session workspace resolution (#1246).

edits.change: Clarify D4's wording to state explicitly it means one fixed detection method per adapter, including per-session workspace resolution, not a single global method.

groups.root_cause: Cross-project session/event scoping dedupe (156aa0fd) must carry forward into the v2 C2 adapter refactor after D8 removes events.md
groups.evidence: 156aa0fd 'fix(737): filter/dedupe correctness - contentType+source scoping, full-content dedupe key' fixed a real cross-project leak in v1. d923716d (adapter refactor) and 6e8556ce (extracting purgeSession) show the dedupe logic was carried into the newer code paths, not dropped.

edits.change: State explicitly that the C2 adapter's session/project scoping inherits 156aa0fd's project-scoped dedupe key, so removing events.md does not reopen the #737-class cross-project leak.

groups.root_cause: ctx_execute has no stated default timeout or cancel path, blocking #1182's cancel-path test
groups.evidence: DECISIONS-r3 does not set a default ctx_execute timeout anywhere in Q1-Q19; this blocks #1182's cancel-path test.

edits.change: Set a fixed default timeout (120s) with a per-call override param, tied to the same AbortSignal mechanism used for #1182's cancel path; add the GP case.

groups.root_cause: No per-agent ctx_* tool-count allow-list exists for context-constrained clients
groups.decision: wont-fix: no evidence any of the 10 target agents enforces a tool-count budget
groups.evidence: No ADR addresses an explicit tool-name allow-list env var; TECH-SPEC's adapter table does not list a tool-count cap for any of the 10 target agents.

edits.change: Close as wont-fix until a specific target agent is shown to enforce a small fixed tool budget.

groups.root_cause: v2's single default exec timeout must explicitly supersede the antigravity-cli adapter-local default
groups.evidence: e4f4379d 'fix(antigravity-cli): default exec timeout under agy + anti-dump rules' already shipped a default timeout scoped to one adapter. Per owner rule (no fallback chains), v2's single global default must replace it, not coexist as a second path.

edits.change: State that v2's single default exec timeout value explicitly supersedes and removes e4f4379d's adapter-local antigravity-cli default.

groups.root_cause: WebFetch allow-list for claude.ai artifacts becomes moot once D10 removes hard denies
groups.evidence: No commit found adding or removing a WebFetch deny-list entry for claude.ai artifacts specifically. D10 (no hard denies) removes the mechanism that would have blocked this, making a special-case allow entry unnecessary by construction.

edits.change: Confirm D10's replacement mechanism permits claude.ai artifact fetches by default, closing this without a special-case allow entry.

groups.root_cause: Windows vitest EPERM hang blocks the v1-KEEP-PASS CI gate
groups.decision: covered-by-test with KEEP-PASS test (fix teardown, do not skip)
groups.evidence: e918eac6 and b3a26354 fixed a related but different Windows EPERM (boot-install shell:true dropping cwd); #995's EPERM is in vitest itself (test DB handles not closed). Owner rule: v1 unit tests stay until v2 passes the 131 KEEP-PASS ones -- the hang must be fixed, not routed around by skipping.

edits.change: Close all sqlite DB handles explicitly in test teardown before process exit, resolving the Windows EPERM hang without skipping any kept test.
